scenes.name: New romantics y la escena del Blitz
scenes.book: Postpunk. Romper todo y empezar de nuevo
scenes.author: Simon Reynolds
scenes.desc: En el club Billy's y luego el Blitz, Rusty Egan pincha Bowie de Berlín, Iggy, Moroder, Kraftwerk, «Being Boiled», Telex y Yellow Magic Orchestra, y Steve Strange guarda la puerta: maquillaje, sombreros españoles y cortes geométricos, fantasía y escapismo tras ocho horas de trabajo. Visage, superbanda de punks fracasados (Ure, Currie, tres de Magazine), con la tristeza sobrenatural de «Fade to Grey»; Spandau Ballet, elitista y nietzscheano antes de volverse soul; Ultravox reformado con Midge Ure y la glacial «Vienna» (1981). Bowie lo corona con «Ashes to Ashes», con Strange vestido de Pierrot. Martin Rushent, con su sello Genetic, llegó a tenerlos a casi todos.

scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
scenes.author: Javier Blánquez (ed.)
scenes.desc: Movimiento londinense que rescata del glam el maquillaje y la pose, con un uso coyuntural de la tecnología: Ultravox (con John Foxx primero), Japan, Visage de Steve Strange, Duran Duran, Spandau Ballet, ABC, la pose kraftwerkiana de Gary Numan y, después, Culture Club.

podcast.title: "Scary Monsters" Video Extra
podcast.body: Steve Strange, who later became the frontman of the New Romantic band Visage, was plucked from London's avant-garde Blitz Club to be an extra in David Bowie's groundbreaking 1980 music video for his "Scary Monsters" album. This early exposure was part of the video's significant cultural impact that helped launch the New Romantic movement. "One of them was Steve Strange who would later head up his own new romantic band called Vizache."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Blitz Kid to Band Frontman
podcast.body: Steve Strange, a prominent figure among the Blitz kids, appeared in David Bowie's "Ashes to Ashes" video. He later went on to front the band Visage, marking his transition from a subculture icon to a musical artist. "Steve Strange, one of the people in that video, would later front of band called Visage, which did okay."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Co-Founder of The Blitz Club
podcast.body: Steve Strange, who did not fully fit with the punk scene, co-founded The Blitz Club in a small London basement in the late 1970s with Rusty Egan. The club paid homage to David Bowie's glam aesthetic and played new music, with Kraftwerk being a constant presence. "dos jóvenes que no encajaban del todo con la rodeaza del punk, Steve Strange y Rastiegan abrieron el blitz."

xref.title: New Romantic Exemplar
xref.body: Visage is highlighted as a prime example of New Romantic music, spearheaded by Steve Strange. Their sound contributed to the evolving electronic and synth-driven landscape of the scene. "A great example of New Romantic music is Vizage, headed up by Steve Strange."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Origin from Blitz Kids Movement
xref.body: Visage was fronted by Steve Strange, who gained recognition as one of the Blitz kids featured in David Bowie's "Ashes to Ashes" video. The band's emergence reflects its roots in the Blitz kids' subculture and the broader New Romantic movement. "Steve Strange, one of the people in that video, would later front of band called Visage, which did okay."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
